k4.disputed_point: Whether Carvana has a history of a distressed exchange or restructuring. The key says there was one in 2023. Answer A reports finding no distressed exchanges and leaves the 2023 exchange out of its debt events.
k4.why: The 2023 restructuring happened. Carvana announced a support agreement on 2023-07-19 with holders of over 90% of its unsecured notes, to cut debt by over $1.2B. The final exchange results on 2023-08-31 put the reduction at over $1.325B. S&P cut Carvana to 'CC' on the proposed exchange and said it was tantamount to default. Answer A looks only at 2025–2026 events. Its Q3 2026 data and the August 2026 Term Loan B refinancing of the 2030 notes show no current default, covenant breach or going-concern language, which matches the key's 'no current' finding. Answer A's statement that it found no distressed exchanges is wrong as a statement about Carvana's history, because it omits the 2023 exchange. The key's 'interest deferral' wording is loose: the new notes paid interest in cash or in kind, and the cash-interest saving was over $455M a year for two years. The key's $1.2B figure is the initial announcement, and the final figure was about $1.3B. Neither point reverses the key. I could not open the Q3 2026 10-Q itself, so I confirmed no current default, covenant breach or going-concern language only from the Q3 2026 release and call material that Answer A cites.

k8.disputed_point: The overall risk label: the key says "Moderate (provisional)", while both answers say "elevated".
k8.why: This is a judgment call, not a checkable fact, and the three sources agree on the underlying facts. Q3 2026 revenue was $8.04B and net income was $483M, up 84% (capital.com, which I opened). The answers cite a 10-Q showing $3.05B cash, $5.12B committed liquidity, roughly $5.2B of debt and covenant compliance. They also cite speculative-grade ratings: S&P BB-/positive, Fitch first-time BB-, and Moody's B1/positive per the answers. The key and the answers also name the same offsetting risks: leverage, reliance on ABS and Ally funding, cyclical used-car and auto-credit exposure, related-party dealings and the short-seller allegations. They differ only on whether the label is "moderate" or "elevated". The key hedges with "provisional" and asks for ratings and the maturity ladder to be confirmed. The answers supply that confirmation, and it shows speculative-grade ratings with positive outlooks. I could not independently confirm the Moody's rating. My search turned up only older Caa1 references, and the Moody's page I opened was empty. So I treat the answers' Moody's figures as unverified. Either label is defensible for a BB-/B1 issuer with improving credit, and none of the sources shows a factual error in the key.
k8.corrected_answer: Moderate (provisional). Profitability and EBITDA are strong and 2023 restructuring risk has receded. Offsetting that are high leverage, dependence on ABS and Ally funding markets, a cyclical used-car and auto-credit exposure, controlling-family related-party dealings and the short-seller accounting allegations. Confirm ratings and the maturity ladder before finalizing. Note: an "elevated" call is also acceptable. It rests on the issuer ratings of BB- (S&P, positive outlook) and BB- (Fitch), the B1/positive Moody's rating the answers report, about $5.2B of debt, and a $2.1B tax receivable agreement liability. It is offset by $3.0B cash, $5.1B committed liquidity and covenant compliance at 2026-09-30.
